description:
INFORMATION AND RAMBLINGSAs somebody who can't stop modding, I've been fiddling about with the inner workings of the game.

It's fun to break open files, edit values or swap/insert lines of code and see what happens, because sometimes genuinely interesting or cool things can be the result. This is a compilation of working alterations I've discovered, tested and created. Thought I would share them with you all.

There are detailed handwritten guides on how to do things below (click the titles) and more will be added as ideas come to life.

LLM Disclaimer:

As a note, I have used ChatGPT to help me along the way. Although I have dabbled with Java (and Python) in the past, I don't have enough experience with coding to be fully self-reliant. It's also a great soundboard for ideas that pop into my head, for confirming whether or not they are possible within the confines of the .jar files and for checking I haven't made mistakes with my alterations, etc. For me, it simply speeds up the process.

The edits I've made are done by hand, as this makes it easier to build guides. Learn by doing and all that!

Everything has been tested multiple times, both during and after creation. Firstly, GPT ran the code within itself to ensure there were no conflicts or incorrect values and that the alterations worked. Then I ran the edit in-game for roughly 3-6 months (depending on what was changed), in case there were unintended effects. This is how I ironed-out any issues. Haven't seen any blatantly obvious problems occurring in the final versions, but I won't stand on a soap box and shout

"How dare you! They are perfect and you're doing it wrong!"

because games are temperamental at the best of times.

Please report any issues you might come across and I'll investigate!

You'll need some extra tools, as listed in the guides with download links. It's all above board and official. No obscure and unknown files. The tools used are Recaf, JDK-25, Windows PowerShell, Notepad++ and sometimes Microforge (a Starsector utility mod, available from this forum). A quick search can verify the legitimacy of these, if needed.

Most edits require digging into the .jar files and making changes using those tools.

Should you wish to stack the .jar edits on top of each other, then use the already-modified .jar file from another edit, in place of the vanilla one in the guides. I've done this, to have all changes together in one game and it works perfectly fine.

I'll continue to alter the first post as I discover and construct them. Bookmark the page, if you wish to check for updates now and again.

Devs and forum members are very welcome to use and/or adapt anything I create for their own purposes. If an edit I've done means it has helped a person in some way, I'm happy to have contributed towards that.

A simple thanks is more than enough.

So, without further ado.[close]

RANDOM GUIDES FOR VARIOUS GAME CHANGES

Click the titles for links to Pastebin guides.

Thicker Campaign Map Circles

Increases the thickness of the circles that surround fleets, stations, derelicts and such on the System and Hyperspace maps.

THICKNESS PREVIEW IMAGE[close]

Works with all factions, vanilla and modded. Takes the colours directly from the .faction files, so it uses whatever RGBA values are in those files.

This scales as you zoom in and out. Zoom in, the circles become thinner and vice versa. Fully customisable thickness, through simple value edits.

Commission-Based UI Colour Schemes

The colour of the player's campaign map circles and UI will dynamically change, depending on what faction they have a Commission with.

For example, if you take a Hegemony Commission, the campaign map entity circles and UI will change to the faction's orange colour scheme. If you resign the Commission, it will automatically revert back to the standard grey (or whatever colour you have changed it to, in the player.faction file). Grab a new Commission, even with a different faction, it changes again!

It uses whatever RGBA values are present in the .faction files, so if you have altered any faction colour schemes (as I have), it will automatically display those colours. No trickery involved, just pointing it in the right direction. Works with all factions, vanilla and modded.

Improved Scan and Survey Missions

Modifies the starting location of missions to the market/system that generated them.

The vanilla game will always calculate the credit reward earned from the 0,0 centre of the sector outwards. So if you take a mission from a system that is in, say, the bottom-left corner and the mission target is in the top-right corner, the code does not take into account the fact that you have to travel across the entire map. You will only be paid as if you were starting your journey from the centre.

Logically, that didn't make sense to me, so this edit changes that calculation. Now the faction market from the system who spawns a mission will be the starting location and the reward calculated properly from there instead. You'll be paid appropriately for the entire journey, from source to target. No more being cheated out of credits!

Works perfectly with the Wide Horizons mod. No idea about other sector-altering mods, as I don't use them. You'll have to test that yourselves.

Also includes additional information on how to edit the mission completion time limit, credit rewards and faction reputation changes.

Hyperspace Nebulae Layers

Adds three moving layers of nebulae to the Hyperspace map. Also disables the "wobble" effect from the background image.

The nebulae sprites are taken from the existing image present in the graphics\terrain folder. No new assets have been added at all. Just some clever code to say "use this image, chop it up, do this and that, put them on X layer in Y manner", all using proper coding.

Each layer uses different speeds, sizes and seeding, to create truly unique nebulae layers. This creates a wonderful and layered moving background effect, to emulate depth, as you travel through Hyperspace.

NEBULAE MOVEMENT PREVIEW VIDEO[close]

Removal of the wobble effect, I would say is necessary. You won't see it, so there is no point in keeping it around to eat up game resources it could be using elsewhere. There is an optional (but recommended) custom background image, that I made from the sprites and darkened, to use for those very brief moments when the background

might

peek through.

As a note, when you zoom in and out, it does go a bit weird as it rearranges the layers to match the zoom level. That can't be avoided. I'll look into it again, but I couldn't figure out how to stop it. If you have any ideas, please feel free to comment.

Realistic Solar Activity

Adds moving effects to stars, to simulate solar activity.

This edit will add UV distortion effects to all stars across the entire game. Basically, the texture will be manipulated into moving around in random spots on the image surface, twisting and distorting. There are no external add-ons put into the game, as it purely utilises what is already available in the Java code.

SOLAR ACTIVITY PREVIEW VIDEO[close]

As a note, I have custom star wraps for my game. The vanilla star wraps are not as detailed as you see in the video, so the effects will be lessened, but it still works. This edit does not add a new wrap, only the visual distortion effect. My versions were recorded to show the effect more clearly.

Personally, I didn't notice any difference with regards to game performance with or without the edit. Tested on a Nexerlin + 250% Wide Horizons sector, alongside all of the other edits with a bunch of extra mods and the game performed exactly the same as usual.

I haven't figured out the best values for each star type yet, as I'm still tweaking them alongside creating other new edits. But below is a handy general list of least-to-most active, based on the typical level of activity, if you want to get a head start by making those changes yourselves.

STAR ACTIVITY LISTWhite Dwarf

Brown Dwarf

Orange Giant / Red Giant

Yellow

Orange

Red Dwarf

Blue Giant / Blue Supergiant / Red Supergiant

Neutron[close]

Hyperspace Storm Control

Adds customisable functionality over Hyperspace Storm behaviour, through an extensive .json configuration file.

This edit provides full control over the Storms on the Hyperspace map, allowing you to adjust how often they appear, how they spread and activate, how they interact with fleets, and how damaging or disruptive they are. The default settings reproduce vanilla behaviour.

Included are various NEW settings, not typically available in the vanilla config. Check the list below for full details.

LIST OF ADJUSTABLE CONFIGURATIONS

Storm Seeding Control

• Change how many storm cells are active when the system is first created.

• Change how many new cells are seeded during later generation cycles.

Storm Generation Speed

• Change how often the underlying storm pattern updates.

• Shorter cycles make the storm layout evolve faster; longer cycles make it more stable.

Storm Chain Reaction Rules

• Change how many neighbouring active cells are required for a storm to spread.

• Add a configurable chance that propagation actually succeeds, rather than always succeeding once the neighbour requirement is met.

Storm Lifecycle Timing

• Control how long a newly-created storm waits before it begins signalling.

• Control how long the warning/signalling phase lasts.

• Control how long a storm takes to fade away after becoming unsupported.

Fleet-Triggered Storm Activation

• Enable or disable fleets prematurely activating signalling storms.

• Change how close a storm must be to activating before a fleet can trigger it.

• Set a minimum fleet size required to trigger activation.

• Set a flat activation chance.

• Optionally scale activation chance according to fleet size or strength.

Fleet-Size Activation Scaling

• Choose how fleet size is measured:

• Ship count

• Fleet points

• Supplies required to recover the fleet

• Set the minimum and maximum fleet values used for scaling.

• Set the minimum and maximum activation chance between those values.

Storm-Strike Eligibility

• Decide whether slow-moving fleets are immune.

• Decide whether fleets currently in battle are immune.

• Set a minimum fleet size required before a fleet can be struck.

• Optionally scale strike chance according to fleet size or strength.

Fleet-Size Strike Scaling

• Use the same three fleet-size measurements:

• Ship count

• Fleet points

• Supplies to recover

• Set minimum and maximum fleet values.

• Set minimum and maximum strike probability.
